# Radoslav Radev Recommends Alternating Push And Pull Exercises In The Same Workout

Radoslav Radev recommends training push and pull exercises together in the same workout, alternating attempts, for better recovery between attempts. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 00:40]

## Details

- He gives the example of planche and front lever: one attempt of planche, rest three to five minutes, one attempt of front lever, rest three to five minutes, then back to planche. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 00:49]
- Alternating gives six or ten minutes rest between planche attempts and between front lever attempts. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 00:59]
- The goal is to finish the workout 70% exhausted, not 100%, so you can still do productive attempts at the end. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 01:22]
- A good workout is one where you can repeat productive attempts on your hardest progression at the end and stop there to save energy for the next workout. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 01:42]
- This method can also be applied to planche and handstand. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 01:18]

## Evidence

- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 00:40 (Radoslav Radev): "Rule number one, train, push, and pull together. If you train plunge [planche] and front lever, don't train them in separate days. Train them in the same workout."
- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 00:49 (Radoslav Radev): "One attempt of plunge [planche], rest three to five minutes. One attempt of front lever, rest three to five minutes and again back to the planche"
- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 00:59 (Radoslav Radev): "you have six or ten minutes rest between the two planches and between the front levers alternate them the whole workout"
- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 01:22 (Radoslav Radev): "the goal is in the end of the workout to not be 100% exhausted to finish the workout 70% exhausted and to can do in the end of the workout also productive attempts"
- vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 01:42 (Radoslav Radev): "if you can repeat also productive attempts on your hardest progression and you stop the workout there rest and save energy for the next workout that means this workout is smart"

## Why This Matters

Better recovery between attempts means better results, and saving energy for the next workout makes each subsequent workout more productive. [src: vid-e4gjJgvWViQ @ 01:04]
